page.h1: HTS Chapter 22: Beverages, Spirits and Vinegar — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Bourbon, Wine, Beer & Ethanol by Country (HTS Ch. 22) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Canada, the EU, UK, Mexico, India, Colombia, Korea, Japan and China charge on U.S. bourbon, wine, beer, ethanol and soft drinks in 2026, and whose approval you need to sell there.

intro: What each large market charges on U.S. beverages, spirits, ethanol and vinegar in 2026, next to what the U.S. shipped there in 2025; the EU counts as one market because its members share one tariff. China is added at the end, although it bought only $82 million in 2025, because it is the market where U.S. whiskey, wine and beer pay the most. For most of the trade the tariff is zero: Canada and Mexico under USMCA, Colombia and Korea under their U.S. trade agreements, and the EU, the UK and Japan on bourbon and other whiskey. India and China are the exceptions. For alcohol, what usually decides access is the buyer’s distribution system and approvals: Canada’s provincial liquor boards, India’s FSSAI and state excise rules, China’s GACC registration and the EU’s VI-1 wine document.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

markets.name: Canada
markets.rule: CUSMA (USMCA) tariff elimination on qualifying U.S. goods; alcohol is sold through provincial liquor boards

2201.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN: 2201.10 free, 2201.90 6.5%.

2202.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN: 2202.10 and 2202.99.90 11%, 2202.91 free.

2203.basis: Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, 2203.00: beer is free under both MFN and CUSMA.

2204.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN: still wine in containers of 2 liters or less 1.87¢/L (up to 13.7% vol) or 4.68¢/L (13.7–14.9%); sparkling wine free.

2205.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN rate not individually verified.

2206.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN rate not individually verified.

2207.normalRate: 4.92¢/L of pure alcohol on some denatured lines
2207.basis: Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026: 2207.10 (undenatured ethanol) free MFN; 2207.20.11 and 2207.20.12 (specially denatured and denatured alcohol) 4.92¢ per liter of absolute ethyl alcohol, other 2207.20 lines free; all free under CUSMA.

2208.normalRate: Whiskey free; vodka 12.28¢/L and gin 4.92¢/L of pure alcohol
2208.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN: whiskies 2208.30 (including bourbon) free; vodka 12.28¢ and gin 4.92¢ per liter of absolute ethyl alcohol.

2209.basis: CUSMA (USMCA) Annex 2-B; Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026, Chapter 22: qualifying U.S. goods enter duty-free. MFN: 9.5%.

profile.headline: Canada is the largest buyer: $1.71 billion of U.S. ethanol and $951 million of soft drinks, all duty-free under CUSMA. Its 25% federal surtax on U.S. wine, beer, spirits and soft drinks ran from March 4 to August 31, 2025; what still blocks U.S. alcohol is the provincial liquor boards, most of which stopped buying it in March 2025, plus Saskatchewan’s 50% levy from September 8, 2026.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Soft drinks, flavored water, energy drinks and other non-alcoholic beverages (incl. non-alcoholic beer) (2202)
profile.tariffNow: Free (CUSMA); 50% Saskatchewan levy on U.S. alcohol

regulator.name: Provincial liquor boards (for alcohol) and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
regulator.requirement: Beer, wine and spirits reach consumers through each province’s liquor board, which must list (buy) the product; most boards have stopped buying U.S. alcohol since March 2025. Labels must meet CFIA’s alcoholic-beverage labelling rules.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Canada import requirements

markets.name: European Union
markets.rule: EU common external tariff (Combined Nomenclature 2026), plus a 0% U.S. quota for some soft drinks under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455

2201.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2201 10 and 2201 90 00.

2202.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2202 10 00, 2202 91 00 and 2202 99 11–19 at 9.6%. Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, Annex III, quota 09.9017 (from July 1, 2026): 0% for 20,000 tonnes a year of U.S. sweetened or flavored waters (2202 10 00), non-alcoholic beer (2202 91 00) and other soft drinks without milk fat (2202 99 19).

2203.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2203 00 01–10 (beer made from malt).

2204.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2204 21 93–98 (still wine in containers of 2 liters or less: €13.1/hl up to 13% vol, €15.4/hl 13–15%), 2204 10 (sparkling, €32/hl), 2204 22 and 2204 29 (bulk wine, €9.9–12.1/hl).

2205.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2205 10 10 (€10.9/hl) and 2205 90 10 (€9/hl), vermouth up to 18% vol.

2206.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2206 00 51–89 (still cider and other fermented drinks, €5.76–7.7/hl) and 2206 00 31–39 (sparkling, €19.2/hl).

2207.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2207 10 00 (€19.2/hl) and 2207 20 00 (€10.2/hl). The EU’s 2013 anti-dumping duty on U.S. bioethanol was repealed in 2019 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2019/765).

2208.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2208 30 11–88 (whiskies, including bourbon 2208 30 11 / 30 19), 2208 60 (vodka), 2208 70 (liqueurs) and most of 2208 90: free. Rum (2208 40) pays €0.6/%vol/hl + €3.2/hl and undenatured ethanol under 80% (2208 90 91–99) €1/%vol/hl.

2209.basis: EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926), conventional duty, CN 2209 00 11–99 (wine vinegar €4.8–6.4/hl, other vinegar €3.84–5.12/hl).

profile.headline: The EU is the biggest market for U.S. bourbon and other spirits ($1.29 billion in 2025, led by the Netherlands, Ireland and Spain) and the second biggest for ethanol. Bourbon, vodka, liqueurs and beer enter duty-free; the EU’s 2025 counter-list would have put 30% on bourbon, wine and almost the whole chapter, but it has been suspended since August 2025 and never applied.
profile.mainProducts: Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208) · Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207)
profile.tariffNow: Free on bourbon & most spirits and beer; ethanol €19.2/hl; wine €13.1–32/hl

regulator.name: European Commission (spirit-drink and wine rules) and member-state customs and excise authorities
regulator.requirement: No pre-market approval for spirits, but they must meet the EU spirit-drink definitions and labelling rules of Regulation (EU) 2019/787; “Bourbon” and “Tennessee whiskey” are reserved for U.S. products (Regulation (EC) No 936/2009). Wine needs a VI-1 document (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2018/273), and the importer must hold excise warehouse or registered-consignee status.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: EU import requirements

markets.name: United Kingdom
markets.rule: UK Global Tariff, plus the duty-free U.S. ethanol quota under the U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal

2201.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2201.

2202.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2202 10 00 00 and 2202 99 19 at 8%; 2202 91 00 90 (non-alcoholic beer, other) free; dairy-fat drinks 4% + £17/100 kg.

2203.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2203 00 01 00 and 2203 00 10 00.

2204.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2204 21 97 (still wine in bottles: £10/hl up to 13% vol, £12/hl 13–15%), 2204 10 98 (sparkling, £26/hl), bulk wine £8.20–10/hl. WTO quotas 05.0097 and 05.0095 (£8.36/hl and £6.69/hl) are open to U.S. wine.

2205.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2205 10 10 00 and 2205 90 10 00.

2206.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2206 00 51 00 (still cider in bottles, £6.40/hl) and 2206 00 31 00 (sparkling, £16/hl).

2207.basis: U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal: quota 05.9750 for U.S. goods of heading 2207 at 0%, 913 million liters for June 30–December 31, 2025 and 1.4 billion liters a year from January 1, 2026 (The United States Preferential Tariff reference document v1.2, under SI 2025/753). On November 13, 2026 about 100.6 million liters of the 2026 quota were left. Above it, UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty: 2207 10 £16/hl, 2207 20 £8.50/hl.

2208.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2208 30 11 00 / 19 00 (bourbon), 2208 30 82 00 (other whiskies), 2208 60 (vodka), 2208 70 (liqueurs), 2208 90 56 00: free. Undenatured ethanol under 80% (2208 90 91–99) pays £0.80/%vol/hl.

2209.basis: UK Global Tariff (UK Trade Tariff, checked November 19, 2026), third-country duty, 2209 00 11 00 (wine vinegar, £5.30/hl) and 2209 00 91 00 (other vinegar, £4.20/hl).

profile.headline: The UK is the third-largest buyer: mostly ethanol ($393 million), then spirits and wine. Since June 30, 2025 U.S. ethanol has entered duty-free within a quota (1.4 billion liters a year from 2026) instead of paying £16 per hectoliter, but the 2026 quota was nearly used up by mid-November. Bourbon, other spirits and beer pay nothing.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208)
profile.tariffNow: Free on spirits & beer; ethanol 0% within the 1.4bn-liter U.S. quota

regulator.name: HM Revenue & Customs (alcohol duty and AWRS) and the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (wine rules)
regulator.requirement: No pre-market approval. Wholesalers must be approved under HMRC’s Alcohol Wholesaler Registration Scheme, and labels must name a UK business; wine shipped to Great Britain no longer needs a VI-1 (Northern Ireland still does). Fuel ethanol counts toward UK targets only if it meets the Renewable Transport Fuel Obligation’s sustainability rules.

markets.name: Mexico
markets.rule: USMCA (T-MEC) tariff elimination on qualifying U.S. goods

2201.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 2201.10 20%, 2201.90.01 10%.

2202.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 2202.10.01 and 2202.99.99 20% plus US$0.36 per kg of sugar.

2203.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 2203.00.01 20%.

2204.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 2204.10 and 2204.21 20%.

2205.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN rate not individually verified.

2206.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN rate not individually verified.

2207.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 2207.10.01 and 2207.20.01 10% plus US$0.36 per kg of sugar.

2208.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods (including 2208.30.04, bourbon and Tennessee whiskey). MFN (LIGIE): whiskies exempt; vodka, rum, gin and liqueurs 20%.

2209.basis: USMCA Annex 2-B, Tariff Schedule of Mexico: 0% on every Chapter 22 fraction for qualifying U.S. goods. MFN (LIGIE): 20%.

profile.headline: Mexico buys U.S. ethanol ($233 million), soft drinks ($148 million) and spirits ($106 million), all duty-free under USMCA. Without USMCA most lines pay 20%. Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. drinks, and its January 2026 tariff increase for non-FTA countries does not touch Chapter 22.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Soft drinks, flavored water, energy drinks and other non-alcoholic beverages (incl. non-alcoholic beer) (2202)

regulator.name: COFEPRIS (Federal Commission for Protection against Sanitary Risks)
regulator.requirement: COFEPRIS oversees the sanitary rules for alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages; the Mexican importer of alcohol must also be on the tax authority’s sector importers’ register.

markets.name: India
markets.rule: India’s customs tariff: basic customs duty plus the agriculture infrastructure and development cess (AIDC); no trade agreement with the U.S.

2201.basis: India Customs Tariff, 2201; a very small U.S. trade, rate not checked line by line.

2202.basis: India Customs Tariff, 2202; a very small U.S. trade, rate not checked line by line.

2203.basis: India Customs Tariff, 2203: 100% basic customs duty; beer is not in the AIDC entry. Taken from an unofficial copy of the schedule; no U.S. beer was shipped in 2025.

2204.basis: India Customs Tariff with AIDC under Notification No. 11/2021-Customs as amended by No. 14/2025 (February 13, 2025): 50% basic customs duty + 100% AIDC on wine (2204).

2205.basis: India Customs Tariff with AIDC under Notification No. 11/2021-Customs as amended by No. 14/2025 (February 13, 2025): 100% AIDC on 2205; basic duty not individually verified.

2206.basis: India Customs Tariff with AIDC under Notification No. 11/2021-Customs as amended by No. 14/2025 (February 13, 2025): 100% AIDC on 2206; basic duty not individually verified.

2207.basis: India Customs Tariff as reported by USDA FAS (India Biofuels Annual, June 2025): 2207.20 denatured ethanol 5% (0% for use in making excisable goods), 2207.10 undenatured 150%. Imports for fuel use are prohibited and other imports need a DGFT licence (DGFT Notification 06/2015-2020 of May 24, 2019).

2208.basis: India Customs Tariff with AIDC under Notification No. 11/2021-Customs as amended by No. 14/2025 (February 13, 2025): bourbon whiskey (2208 30 11 and 2208 30 91) 50% basic duty + 50% AIDC since February 13, 2025 (150% before); other whiskies and spirits 50% + 100% AIDC.

2209.basis: India Customs Tariff, 2209; a very small U.S. trade, rate not checked line by line.

profile.headline: India buys mostly U.S. ethanol ($409 million) and some spirits ($26 million). Bourbon pays 100% since India cut its cess in February 2025, still the highest rate among large buyers; other spirits and wine pay 150%. Ethanol may not be imported for fuel use, and the February 2026 U.S.–India framework names wine and spirits for cuts that have not yet been published.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208)

regulator.name: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
regulator.requirement: Imported beer, wine and spirits must meet the Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulations, 2018 and pass FSSAI import clearance. Non-fuel ethanol imports need a DGFT licence.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: India import requirements

markets.name: Colombia
markets.rule: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement tariff elimination; countervailing duty on U.S. fuel ethanol

2201.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods; water phased out by 2021.

2202.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods.

2203.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods (beer duty-free since 2012). MFN from WTO/World Bank WITS (TRAINS), 2023.

2204.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods (wine duty-free since 2012). MFN from WITS (TRAINS), 2023.

2205.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods.

2206.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods.

2207.rate: Free (TPA); fuel ethanol also US$0.066/kg CVD
2207.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods (2207.10 from 2012, 2207.20 from 2016). Countervailing duty of US$0.06646 per kg net on U.S. fuel ethanol (2207.20.00.10), imposed by MinCIT Resolution 069 of 2020 and kept for five years by Resolution 044 of March 13, 2023; it is charged on top of the TPA rate. MFN from WITS (TRAINS), 2023.

2208.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods (whiskey, vodka and rum duty-free since January 1, 2021). MFN from WITS (TRAINS), 2023.

2209.basis: U.S.–Colombia Trade Promotion Agreement, Annex 2.3 (Colombia’s schedule): duty-free for U.S. goods.

profile.headline: Colombia is almost entirely an ethanol market ($352 million in 2025). U.S. ethanol, spirits, wine and beer all enter duty-free under the TPA, but Colombia has charged a countervailing duty of US$0.06646 per kilogram on U.S. fuel ethanol since 2020, extended in March 2023 for five years.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208)
profile.tariffNow: Free (TPA); CVD on U.S. fuel ethanol

regulator.name: INVIMA (National Food and Drug Surveillance Institute)
regulator.requirement: Alcoholic beverages need an INVIMA sanitary registration before they can be sold (Decree 1686 of 2012).

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Colombia import requirements

markets.name: South Korea
markets.rule: KORUS FTA tariff elimination on qualifying U.S. goods; every Chapter 22 line is now duty-free

2201.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: duty-free since 2016 or 2021 depending on the line.

2202.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: 2202.10 free since 2012; other lines since 2016 or 2021.

2203.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: beer duty-free since January 1, 2018.

2204.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: wine duty-free since March 15, 2012.

2205.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012.

2206.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012.

2207.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: denatured ethanol (2207.20) free since 2012; undenatured ethanol (2207.10, base rates 10–270%) free since January 1, 2026.

2208.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: bourbon (2208.30.20) free since 2012, other whiskies since January 1, 2016.

2209.basis: KORUS FTA, Annex 2-B (Tariff Schedule of Korea), in force March 15, 2012: duty-free since 2016 or 2021 depending on the line.

profile.headline: Korea buys U.S. ethanol ($207 million), wine ($50 million) and beer ($44 million). Since the last undenatured-ethanol lines reached zero on January 1, 2026, every Chapter 22 good of U.S. origin enters duty-free under KORUS; without it, beer would pay 30%, whiskey 20% and wine 15%.
profile.mainProducts: Ethyl alcohol (undenatured 80%+ and denatured), incl. fuel ethanol (2207) · Wine of fresh grapes (still and sparkling) and grape must (2204)

regulator.name: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS)
regulator.requirement: Every shipment of beverages or alcohol is reported to MFDS for imported-food inspection, and the overseas manufacturer must be registered with MFDS before export.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: South Korea import requirements

markets.name: Japan
markets.rule: Japan’s tariff, with U.S.–Japan Trade Agreement (USJTA) rates on wine, most soft drinks, vinegar and undenatured ethanol

2201.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: 2201.10 3% (no USJTA rate), 2201.90 free.

2202.rate: Free on most (USJTA); 9.6–13.4% on flavored waters
2202.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: USJTA rate free on 2202.99 and on non-alcoholic beer without sugar (2202.91.200); 2202.10 (sweetened or flavored waters) and sugared non-alcoholic beer pay the WTO rate of 9.6–13.4%.

2203.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: beer 2203 free (WTO rate).

2204.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: USJTA rate free on sparkling (2204.10), still (2204.21) and bulk (2204.22, 2204.29) wine; WTO rate 15% or ¥125 per liter, whichever is less, with a ¥67 minimum, on bottled still wine.

2205.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: 2205.10 vermouth in containers of 2 liters or less; whether a USJTA rate applies was not individually verified.

2206.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: cider, mead and sake lines carry specific duties (sake ¥70.40 per liter general rate); the U.S. rate was not individually verified.

2207.rate: 1.8% (USJTA) undenatured; free for ETBE and industrial uses
2207.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: undenatured ethanol of 90% or more (2207.10.199) 1.8% under USJTA, 10% otherwise; biomass ethanol for ETBE and listed industrial uses free; denatured ethanol (2207.20) 27.2% (no USJTA rate).

2208.rate: Free on whiskey (other spirits not individually verified)
2208.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: whiskies 2208.30 free.

2209.basis: Japan’s Tariff Schedule as of October 31, 2026, Chapter 22: vinegar free under USJTA; WTO rate 7.5%.

profile.headline: Japan buys U.S. wine ($92 million), spirits ($69 million) and bottled water ($31 million). U.S. wine now enters duty-free under the U.S.–Japan Trade Agreement instead of the normal 15% or ¥125 per liter, and whiskey and beer are free for everyone. Japan has also pledged to buy U.S. bioethanol as part of its 2025 purchase goals.
profile.mainProducts: Wine of fresh grapes (still and sparkling) and grape must (2204) · Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208)
profile.tariffNow: Free on wine, whiskey & beer; ethanol mostly 1.8% or free

regulator.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
regulator.requirement: Every shipment of beverages or alcohol needs an import notification to an MHLW quarantine station under the Food Sanitation Act (Article 27).

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: Japan import requirements

markets.name: China
markets.rule: China’s normal tariff plus its 2018–19 counter-tariffs (unless excluded) and its 2025 extra 10% on all U.S. goods

profile.headline: China bought $152 million of U.S. Chapter 22 goods in 2024 and $82 million in 2025, mostly whiskey ($27 million), wine ($27 million) and beer ($15 million). U.S. whiskey pays about 40% (5% + 25% + 10%) and wine about 64% without an exclusion, while all 30 Chapter 22 lines are on China’s September 2026 list of U.S. goods recommended for lower tariffs.
profile.mainProducts: Spirits, liqueurs and other spirituous beverages (whisky, vodka, gin, rum, tequila, brandy) (2208) · Wine of fresh grapes (still and sparkling) and grape must (2204)
profile.tariffNow: Normal rate + 25% (2018–19, unless excluded) + 10%; wine also +15%

regulator.name: General Administration of Customs of China (GACC)
regulator.requirement: The U.S. producer must be registered with GACC as an overseas food manufacturer (Decree No. 248) before shipping, and labels must be in Chinese; TTB’s consolidated wine export certificate covers China’s certificate requirements for wine.

countryGuide.label: Country Commercial Guide: China import requirements

2201.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (5%), 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2202.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (5%), Section 301 counter-tariff of 25% (2202.10) or 27.5% (2202.91, 2202.99) unless excluded, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2203.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (beer 0%), 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2204.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (14% sparkling and bottled still wine, 20% bulk), plus the 15% China has charged on U.S. wine since April 2, 2018 (answering the U.S. Section 232 tariffs; no exclusion process), plus the 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion (10% on bulk wine), plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2205.basis: China 2026 Tariff Adjustment Plan: vermouth (2205.10) provisional rate 30% (MFN 65%), plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026); which 2018–19 counter-tariffs apply was not individually verified.

2206.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026); a very small group, check the national line.

2207.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (2207.10 40%, 2207.20 30%), the 15% 2018 counter-tariff on denatured ethanol (Section 232 response), the 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2208.basis: Tariff Commission Announcement No. 1 of 2026: 5% provisional rate on whisky (2208.30.00) from February 2, 2026, for all origins; plus the 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion (also on other spirits, 2208.40–2208.90), plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

2209.basis: China Customs Tariff 2026 (5%), 25% Section 301 counter-tariff (2018–19 lists, rates since February 14, 2020) unless the importer holds an exclusion, plus the extra 10% on all U.S. goods (Tariff Commission Announcement No. 7 of 2025; 24 more points suspended to January 10, 2027 by Announcement No. 6 of 2026).

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in 2026: the EU Combined Nomenclature 2026 (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1926) with Regulation (EU) 2026/1455; the UK Trade Tariff (checked November 19, 2026); Canada’s Customs Tariff 2026; Japan’s Tariff Schedule of October 31, 2026; China’s 2026 tariff and its counter-tariff announcements; India’s customs tariff with Notification No. 14/2025; and, for Mexico, Colombia and Korea, the USMCA, TPA and KORUS schedules.

Each cell names the products that carry most of the trade in that group (bourbon and other whiskey in 2208, still bottled wine in 2204, fuel and industrial ethanol in 2207). Many alcohol duties are specific (per hectoliter, per liter or per liter of pure alcohol), so they do not convert to one percentage. Cells marked “not individually verified” are small groups where the line rate was not checked.
Trade-agreement rates apply only to goods that meet the agreement’s rules of origin; the normal (MFN) rate is shown beside them where it was checked. Quota rates apply only while the quota lasts.
Excise taxes, VAT and provincial or state markups on alcohol are not tariffs and are left out; so are Canada’s provincial liquor-store bans, which are on Tariff updates.

China’s cells add its 2018 counter-tariffs (15% answering U.S. Section 232 on wine and denatured ethanol; 25–27.5% answering Section 301 on almost all Chapter 22 lines, waived only for buyers holding an exclusion) and its extra 10% on all U.S. goods to its normal rate.
National 8–10-digit lines can set a different rate than the one shown. Check the market’s own schedule before relying on this page for a transaction.
